headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a Shower Storage Niche
articleBody:
A recessed niche offers clean organization, but minor installation errors can trigger leaks or awkward tile cuts. Here are common pitfalls homeowners encounter during bathroom updates and how to steer clear of them.

- Using drywall or regular green board: Standard drywall breaks down when exposed to moisture. Always use an approved waterproof backing material or a prefabricated sealed unit.
- Installing a perfectly level sill: A flat sill lets soapy water sit and pool. Ensure the bottom shelf slopes slightly forward so runoff flows freely toward the shower drain.
- Leaving corners and seams unsealed: Gaps in the waterproofing membrane invite moisture behind the tile. Carefully seal all internal corners, penetrations, and transitions into the main wall.
- Ignoring stud layouts and plumbing runs: Discovering vent pipes or supply lines halfway through demo delays work. Verify in-wall framing and mechanicals before choosing your final niche spot.
- Overlooking tile and trim dimensions: Not planning tile sizing leaves tiny, awkward slivers. Lay out full tiles beforehand to match grout lines naturally.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
Taking shortcuts on behind-the-wall preparation almost always leads to moisture issues later. Ensuring proper framing and continuous waterproofing protects your investment.
